fatal_errors: The proposed ambient-temperature tensile study does not reconstruct the temperature-dependent single-crystal compression experiments that revealed cryogenic inertial dulling and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier strengthening.

It treats nominal atomic-size mismatch as equivalent to local lattice distortion, whereas the target mechanism was tested using DFT mean-square atomic displacement and showed composition-specific deviations potentially related to magnetism.
It omits the distinct low-temperature phonon-drag/inertial mechanism and elevated-temperature Mn/Fe-dependent Cottrell-type solute pinning.
No prior evidence is cited despite the request for evidence supporting the hypothesis.
explanation: The response identifies an important part of the target: composition-dependent local lattice distortion can impede dislocation glide and raise strength, with the equiatomic quinary alloy used as a baseline. Its proposed composition series and correlation-based falsification test are scientifically plausible. However, it captures only the room-temperature solid-solution-strengthening component. It does not reproduce the controlled [1̄23] single-crystal compression, CRSS measurements from 9–1373 K, strain-rate jumps, thermal-activation fitting, TEM dissociation-width test, or MSAD scaling. Consequently, it misses the three-regime mechanism: thermally activated glide and inertial dulling at cryogenic temperatures, MSAD-governed intrinsic strength, and Mn/Fe-dependent dynamic solute pinning at high temperature. The predictions are also underspecified and introduce ductility without a corresponding target result.
